title: Ledgy: Junior Finance & Billing Associate
description:
Headquarters:  Germany (Remote); London, United Kingdom; Poland (Remote); Romania (Remote); Spain (Remote)
 

  At Ledgy, we’re on a mission to make Europe a powerhouse of entrepreneurship by building a modern, tech-driven equity management and financial reporting platform for private and public companies. In 2026, we aim to be the leading provider for European IPOs and reporting for share-based payments. We are a value-based company with a core focus on being humble, transparent, ambitious and impactful, all in order to delivery the best experience for our customers and end users. 
 We are proud to partner with some of the world’s leading investors. New Enterprise Associates led our  $22m Series B  round in 2022, with Philip Chopin joining Sequoia’s Luciana Lixandru on our board. 
 We were founded in Switzerland in 2017 and today we operate globally from offices in Zurich and London. We encourage diversity and are an international team coming from 26 different countries and speaking 25 different languages. 
      About the role  
 As Junior Finance and Billing Associate you own billing operations, pre-accounting, and day-to-day finance tasks for our four entities across Ledgy. 
 You report to the Finance Lead and work closely with Revenue Operations, Sales, Customer Success and our external accounting partners. This is a role with real ownership: billing is yours from day one and you will grow to own key work streams in international accounting and finance operations. 
  What you'll do  
  Billing operations  
 
 Own the full billing cycle end to end: set up subscriptions, coordinate invoices and credit note issuing, and manage renewals on time and accurately through our billing platform (currently Stripe) 
 Make sure billing data, contracts and invoicing terms are kept in sync with tools used by Sales and Customer Success 
 Follow up on open receivables, reconcile incoming payments and coordinate dunning 
 Answer customer billing questions from the Customer Support team and resolve disputes and corrections in a timely manner 
 Document billing processes and spot where automation and improvements can reduce manual work 
 
  Pre-accounting support  
 
 Prepare and match supplier invoices, expense receipts and bank transactions for the monthly close of 4 entities 
 Perform basic reconciliations and prepare clean documentation for our external accountants 
 Support month-end tasks, such as accruals and deferrals preparation 
 
  Finance team support  
 
 Help with ad hoc finance tasks: reporting inputs, audit and tax filing requests, credit cards management, and document collection 
 Support payroll queries from the team 
 Keep finance records organized and audit-ready 
 
  What you bring  
 
 2–3 years of experience in billing, accounts receivable, bookkeeping or accounting, and a degree in finance, accounting, business or similar 
 Familiarity with billing, payment or accounting tools (for example Stripe, Rillet or a similar system) 
 Strong attention to detail and a habit of double-checking numbers 
 Solid Excel or Google Sheets skills, and familiarity with standard AI tools such as Claude Cowork 
 Basic understanding of double-entry bookkeeping and VAT 
 Excellent written and spoken English; you are comfortable explaining billing questions to customers and colleagues 
 A structured, reliable way of working: you meet deadlines and flag issues early 
 Curiosity and willingness to learn, and to take ownership of a process 
 Interest in a professional path within startup operations 
 
  Nice to have  
 
 Experience with a SaaS or subscription business and recurring billing 
 Exposure to cross-European accounting systems, such as DATEV or Abacus 
 Exposure to multi-entity or multi-currency accounting 
 German, or another European language 
 Interest in automating repetitive finance work

Pay within the range reflects your skills, experience and the scope of the role, and is set using objective criteria applied consistently across the team. Certain roles are also eligible for additional rewards including variable pay under the applicable plan. Ledgy offers equity through our employee option plan. Benefits offered vary by country and type of employment.   Spain pay range   €49.000  —  €64.000 EUR

title: Cadence Health: Medical Assistant
description:

  Cadence is the clinical AI company automating the treatment of chronic disease. Its Clinical Intelligence takes on the routine, high-volume work of chronic care – monitoring patients, surfacing risks, and coordinating action – so clinicians can focus on the decisions that require them. Grounded in partnerships with more than 20 leading health systems, deep EMR integrations, dedicated medical group, and experience serving a population of more than 100,000 patients, the system learns from real-world care delivery, improving as it scales. Cadence has been recognized by TIME as one of the Top 100 HealthTech Companies and by LinkedIn as a Top Startup (#4, 2025).    The Role  
 We’re hiring a Clinical Navigator (Medical Assistant) to deliver virtual chronic care support for Medicare patients enrolled in Cadence care programs. 
 Clinical Navigators deliver proactive, patient-centered outreach and follow-through. Depending on program needs, this role includes structured patient check-ins, coaching and goal-setting, care coordination to close gaps in care, and addressing barriers such as access to resources, transportation, or medication refills. Clinical Navigators document patient interactions in the Cadence platform and collaborate closely with the clinical team to escalate concerns and coordinate next steps, ensuring patients feel supported, informed, and engaged throughout their care journey. 
  Schedule  
 This is a full-time, remote position based in the United States. Standard working hours are Monday through Friday, from 8am to 5pm or 9am to 6pm in your local time zone. 
  What You’ll Do  
 
 Conduct outbound telephonic patient outreach and provide one-on-one coaching and support to patients managing chronic conditions, including but not limited to type 2 diabetes, hypertension, and cardiovascular disease. 
 Help patients execute personalized care plans and achieve their goals by providing education and coaching focused on behavior modification, nutrition, physical activity, and self-management strategies using evidence-based techniques such as motivational interviewing and SMART goals. 
 Conduct comprehensive assessments of patients' health status, lifestyle behaviors, nutritional habits, and readiness to change. 
 Educate patients on disease management, medication adherence, symptom recognition, and prevention strategies, and execute care delivery tasks in accordance with Cadence clinical policies and established protocols, under appropriate clinical supervision. 
 Monitor patients' progress, adherence to treatment plans, and health outcomes through regular check-ins and remote monitoring tools. 
 Document patient interactions, outcomes, and follow-up plans in the Cadence platform; identify barriers to care (including social needs) and connect patients with resources or internal support pathways. 
 Collaborate in real time with clinicians and patient support teams using tools such as our Cadence Platform, Google Workspace, and Slack, and contribute feedback to improve workflows in a fast-moving, change-oriented environment.

They are not to be construed as an exhaustive list of job duties performed by personnel in this classification. Other job related duties may be assigned by management.

 A clinician who thrives at the intersection of rigorous care standards and a care delivery model that is still being built.

 Disciplined in documentation and follow-through, with the attention to detail required for accurate clinical records in a remote environment. 
 Reliable and consistent in schedule adherence, with the interpersonal communication skills to build trust with patients over the phone. 
 Comfortable working independently in a remote, fast-paced environment with evolving workflows, and tech-savvy enough to navigate and troubleshoot multiple systems simultaneously while keeping patients engaged. 
 Comfortable using AI-assisted clinical tools (such as Gemini or Open Evidence) to support patient interactions and surface relevant clinical context, while maintaining clinical judgment as the primary guide for every patient decision. 
 Biased toward action - you bring clinical authority to every interaction, make the call when it counts, and take ownership of outcomes.

The client's philosophy is simple: every project starts with a clear plan that resolves layout, levels, materials, and planting before anything is built - so construction happens without guesswork, miscommunication, or costly rework.  The studio's process runs in two stages: a concept report developed locally with the client, followed by detailed construction drawings. We're growing our team to bring the construction drawing stage in-house on an offshore basis, freeing up our local design team to focus on new client work while drawings progress in the background.    ROLE OVERVIEW:  We're looking for a skilled CAD draftsperson to take finalised landscape design concepts and turn them into accurate, buildable construction drawing sets. This is a genuine long-term team role, not a one-off gig - we're investing in someone who wants to grow with the business, not just complete tasks.  The ideal candidate is confident in producing both construction drawings and photorealistic renders, giving us a single point of contact who can carry a project from concept through to construction-ready documentation.    RESPONSIBILITIES:   Convert approved concept designs into detailed, accurate construction drawing sets (setout plans, levels, sections, details, planting plans, and material schedules).  Work primarily in Vectorworks to ensure drawings are consistent with the client's existing file standards and templates.  Produce photorealistic or presentation-quality renders to support client approvals, where required.  Liaise with Drew and the local design team to clarify design intent, resolve details, and incorporate feedback.  Maintain drawing accuracy for levels, drainage falls, and material junctions so drawings are genuinely buildable on site.  Manage your own workflow and deadlines across multiple concurrent projects, flagging risks or delays early.  Keep drawing files, layers, and naming conventions organised and consistent across projects.  
  Proven, verifiable proficiency in Vectorworks is strongly preferred.  Candidates with strong experience in SketchUp, Revit, or AutoCAD will also be considered - we're open to supporting a transition to Vectorworks. Who You Are  You are a consultative technical advisor who makes  Claravine  work inside customers' real technology stacks and keeps it working as their businesses change. You see the gap between what a customer uses today and what they could be doing, and you can explain that gap to executives and operations teams alike.  As a Solutions Architect (SA), you will own the technical solution for a book of enterprise accounts, from discovery through a validated build.  This is an advisory role with hands-on build responsibility. You will be prescriptive about the decisions a customer needs to make, including the sequence, the trade-offs, and their technical consequences, and you will give a recommended starting point. The customer owns the final content of their taxonomy. You make sure they can make those decisions early, with confidence, and build something that lasts. You will work closely with Customer Success, our Forward-Deployed Product Managers, Enablement, Support, and Product.  What You'll Do  Design and deliver the right solution  
 Lead technical discovery: understand the customer's workflow from brief to reporting, what consumes  Claravine  data downstream, and what that system requires. 
 Solve the business requirement rather than the stated request, and have that conversation openly when the two differ. 
 Design solutions that the customer's own administrator can maintain and that survive their next reorganization. 
 Build to a high standard (structure, naming, testing, and documentation) and validate against real customer data before declaring a build complete. 
 Surface scope change, risk, and blockers early instead of absorbing them quietly. 
  Advise customers through the decisions that stall implementations  
 Guide customers through the taxonomy and governance decisions they need to settle (structure, granularity, ownership, approvals, and enforcement) using  Claravine 's decision guides and a recommended starting point. 
 Bring these decisions forward to kickoff and discovery, where they are cheap, rather than letting them block the build. 
 Challenge what customers bring instead of overlaying  Claravine  on top of a broken process, and identify the organizational problem when it is presented as a technical one. 
 Document the why behind every design decision as it is made. 
  Drive value after go-live  
 Maintain current-state documentation for each account you own: what is built, what is used, and what is dormant. 
 Identify the top unrealized capabilities for every account and make that gap visible through repeatable plays, run alongside the Customer Success Manager (CSM). 
 Take over build support from our Forward-Deployed Product Managers at handoff and support incremental growth into new teams, business units, and use cases. 
  Be the technical authority on the platform and the ecosystem  
 Know what the platform does and where it stops, and never commit the product to behavior it does not have. 
 Design against the constraints of adjacent systems such as Adobe Analytics, Google Analytics 4 (GA4), ad platforms, digital asset management (DAM) and product information management (PIM) systems, customer data platforms (CDPs), data warehouses, and work management tools. 
 Resolve complex technical questions and Tier 2 issues, routing routine requests to Support and true defects to Engineering with clear evidence. 
  Make the product and the team better

title: Airbnb: Senior Manager, Technical Brand & Content
description:
Headquarters:  Remote - United States 
 

   Airbnb was born in 2007 when two hosts welcomed three guests to their San Francisco home, and has since grown to over 5 million hosts who have welcomed over 2 billion guest arrivals in almost every country across the globe. Every day, hosts offer unique stays and experiences that make it possible for guests to connect with communities in a more authentic way.     The Community You Will Join:  
 Airbnb’s mission is to create a world where people can Belong Anywhere. As we work to achieve that mission, our cross functional Tech Operations and Programs team helps enable Tech organizations to execute and deliver on high impact programs and initiatives.  
  The Difference You Will Make:  
 You will decide what the engineering world knows about Airbnb. 
 
 Our engineers solve hard problems at scale across infrastructure, data, and applied AI — and they write about that work well. Almost none of the engineers we'd most like to hire have ever seen it. 
 You'll change that, and the change is measurable. A year in, senior candidates should arrive already able to describe our technical work accurately, because they found it before we found them. Our engineers should be recognised names in their fields rather than anonymous authors. Airbnb should be the source people cite on at least one technical domain. And the strongest engineers in the market should have a reason to choose us that has nothing to do with the offer. 
 That is a rare kind of impact for this discipline. Most tech brand roles are asked to manufacture credibility that isn't there. Here the engineering is genuinely strong and already documented — the gap is that it doesn't travel. You'd be building the function that closes it, with real autonomy, very little inherited process, and direct access to engineering leaders and our CTO. 
 
  A Typical Day:  
 
 Own the editorial engine. Run the Airbnb Tech Blog end to end: sourcing topics from teams, coaching engineer-authors, editing to a high bar, and moving posts through legal, security and comms review without letting them stall. Set and hold a publishing rhythm the org can rely on. 
 Find the cross-team narratives. Our biggest gap is that individually strong posts never add up to a story. You'll work across orgs to identify the themes that connect work from multiple teams, and publish them as connected sets — while each domain keeps publishing in depth for its own specialists. 
 Build our voices. Help our engineers and technical leaders develop genuine public presence: bylines, talks, speaker coaching, and a pipeline of new voices. This includes partnering closely with our CTO to establish his public technical presence. 
 Own distribution. Establish our canonical home on an Airbnb-owned domain, stand up the surfaces we're missing including video, and decide what our social channels are for. Publishing well and distributing poorly is the pattern we're here to break. 
 Run our external presence. Set conference and event strategy — where we speak, where we sponsor, where we skip — and manage what we host ourselves. Own our academic collaborations and technical media relationships, and the budget and vendors behind all of it. 
 Steward our open source presence. Make sure what Airbnb claims publicly is accurate and actually maintained, and that the projects carrying our name reflect how we want to be seen. 
 Prove it works. Partner with Talent Acquisition to connect this work to hiring outcomes — inbound share of the senior pipeline, offer acceptance at staff level and above in ML and infrastructure — and be honest about what is and isn't attributable. 
 
  Your Expertise:  
 
 Substantial experience in technical content, developer relations, engineering communications or technical editorial — including time spent working directly with engineers, not adjacent to them. 
 Technical fluency. You don't need to write production code, but you need to hold your own in a systems design conversation, read a design doc, and judge whether a draft post says anything real. Credibility with staff engineers is the difference between this role working and not working. 
 Editorial judgment and hands-on craft. You can edit an engineer's draft into something sharper without flattening their voice, and you know the difference between a post that teaches something and one that announces something. 
 Influence without authority. Nothing you need is owned by you. You've built systems and incentives that got busy senior people to produce, rather than relying on persistence. 
 Program discipline. You've owned events, budgets and vendors end to end, and you're comfortable with the unglamorous half of the job. 
 Measurement literacy. You connect brand work to funnel outcomes, and you're straight about the limits of attribution rather than reaching for impressions. 
 Judgment on risk. You've navigated legal and security review, and you know what shouldn't be published as well as what should.

description:

   We're transforming the grocery industry  
  At Instacart, we invite the world to share love through food because we believe everyone should have access to the food they love and more time to enjoy it together. Where others see a simple need for grocery delivery, we see exciting complexity and endless opportunity to serve the varied needs of our community. We work to deliver an essential service that customers rely on to get their groceries and household goods, while also offering safe and flexible earnings opportunities to Instacart Personal Shoppers.  
 Instacart has become a lifeline for millions of people, and we’re building the team to help push our shopping cart forward. If you’re ready to do the best work of your life, come join our table. 
  Instacart is a Flex First team   
 There’s no one-size fits all approach to how we do our best work. Our employees have the flexibility to choose where they do their best work—whether it’s from home, an office, or your favorite coffee shop—while staying connected and building community through regular in-person events.  Learn more about our flexible approach to where we work.     Overview  
 The Advertiser Optimization team is the decision-making engine of Instacart's $1B+ ads business. We own the systems responsible for Bidding, Pacing, Budgeting, Targeting and advertiser-facing recommendations - converting stated advertiser goals into real-time auction actions. Our mission is to maximize realized Advertiser Value by deciding when to participate, how much to bid, and how fast to spend, all while carefully balancing User Experience and Platform Revenue. 
   
 We are looking for an Applied Research Scientist II with a strong quantitative background to join our team. In this role, you will apply your expertise in operational research, mathematics, statistics, economics, or a related field to help build and refine the algorithmic systems that power how Instacart's advertising marketplace operates. You'll work alongside a talented team of scientists and engineers, contributing to production systems that have real, measurable impact on a scaled ads platform. If you're excited by the intersection of rigorous quantitative thinking and large-scale engineering, this is the role for you.

 Develop and evaluate models and algorithms for ads bidding, pacing, and budgeting, applying your training in operational research, mathematics, statistics, economics, or a related quantitative discipline to solve complex marketplace problems at scale. 
 Collaborate closely with senior scientists, engineers and product managers to translate well-defined marketplace questions into mathematical formulations, implement analyses and prototypes, design experiments, and interpret results using large-scale data. 
 Contribute to production systems through algorithm implementation, validation, and monitoring, progressively taking ownership of well-scoped projects from initial hypothesis through measurable impact. 
 Operate in a fast-paced, constantly evolving environment where the ads marketplace shifts quickly — you'll need to balance rigor with speed, and thrive when priorities change and new challenges emerge. 
 Communicate assumptions, findings, and limitations clearly to both technical and cross-functional partners, helping the team make better decisions through transparency and analytical clarity.

 Strong analytical and communication skills, including the ability to explain assumptions, methodologies, results, and limitations to both technical and cross-functional audiences.
